about: Normative HTML semantics for ExpressiveCSS components. This data file is the single source of truth: SEMANTICS.md is generated from it by scripts/gen-semantics.mjs, and tests/semantics.test.js enforces it. CONTEXT.md defines the vocabulary.
scope: Element choice, landmark structure, and the ARIA that element choice implies. Keyboard interaction, focus management and colour contrast are deliberately out of scope.
rules: Static semantics are the page author's; dynamic state is the framework's. See CONTEXT.md for both terms.

A component may declare a composite role only if its keyboard contract is implemented and tested. Tabs and Carousel do not qualify: tabs are navigation (`<nav>` + anchors + `aria-current`), not a `tablist`.
Icons are `<span class="material-symbols" aria-hidden="true">`. `<i>` keeps working but is undocumented.
`<nav>` is for genuine navigation only, and every one carries a required `aria-label`. Card action rows and toolbars are not navigation.
Every user-facing string the framework generates has an `i18n` option.

ruleKinds.forbid: selector must match nothing in a checked example
ruleKinds.require-attr: every element matching selector must carry attr (and equal `equals`, when given)

autocomplete.note: Swept 0.8.0. The combobox it builds is checked at runtime in tests/autocomplete.test.js.

rules.message: The suggestion list is a listbox; every entry in it is an option.
A card’s action row is buttons, not destinations. <nav> is a landmark, and one per card floods the landmark list.

character-counter.note: Swept 0.8.0. Checked at runtime in tests/character-counter.test.js.

rules.message: The count changes as the user types, so it has to be a live region or the remaining characters are never announced.

chips.note: Swept 0.8.0. The four Material 3 chip types plus a non-interactive display chip, across three root elements; the delete affordance is a real button.

rules.message: A chip is <span> (display), <button> (assist/suggestion/input), or <label> (filter). Never <div>.
A display chip is not a control and must not be in the tab order. Put the action on a nested <button>.
The chip delete affordance is a control: use <button type="button" class="close">, not <i> or <span>.
A <button> inside a form defaults to type=submit. Chip delete buttons must set type="button".
The delete button contains only an icon, so it needs an accessible name naming the chip it removes.
<i> means idiomatic text, not icon. Use <span class="material-symbols" aria-hidden="true">.
A ligature icon is read aloud verbatim. Decorative icons inside a labelled control must be aria-hidden.
A filter chip is <input type="checkbox"> + <label class="chip">; the label must point at its input.
A checkbox must be inside its <label> or carry an id a label points at.
A fieldset without a legend groups controls visually but names nothing.
A control inside a control is not valid HTML and gives two overlapping hit targets. Use a <label> styled as a button.
The path field only ever displays what the file input holds; leaving it writable offers an edit that is discarded.

forms/input-fields.note: Swept 0.8.0. .field is the container; icons name their side and are hidden; supporting text is linked to the control it describes.

rules.message: The field container is `.field`. `.input-field` matches nothing in the sheet - the only `.input-field` rule is `.chips.input-field`.
<i> means idiomatic text, not icon. Use <span class="material-symbols">.
The ligature is read aloud. A field icon is decoration; the label names the control.
A field icon must name its side with .prefix or .suffix. The positional fallback counts elements of the same *type*, which only ever worked for <i>.
The floating label sits after the control, so it cannot wrap it - association has to be explicit.
Without an id the label has nothing to point at.
Supporting and error text has to be referenceable to be announced with the control.
A field with supporting text must point at it with aria-describedby, or the text is never read out with the control.

forms/radio-buttons.note: Swept 0.8.0. A radio is one of a set, and the set needs a name.

rules.message: A radio only means something as one of a group, and the group needs a <fieldset> with a <legend> to name the question being answered.
A radio must be inside its <label> or carry an id a label points at.
A range announces only its value unless something names it.

forms/select.note: Swept 0.8.0. The listbox FormSelect builds is checked at runtime in tests/select.test.js.

rules.message: role=option promises a selection state. Without aria-selected the listbox never says which entry is chosen.
A switch is a <label> wrapping its checkbox - that is what makes the text its accessible name.
On/off captions inside the label are folded into the accessible name, which then reads "Off On". Hide them and let the label text name the switch.

icons-material-design.note: Rules written, sweep not started. ~100 <i class="material-icons"> examples remain in llm.md.

rules.message: <i> means idiomatic text. The canonical icon element is <span class="material-symbols">.
The ligature is text and is announced. Decorative icons carry aria-hidden="true"; the control carries the label.

aria-selected is not valid on a listitem. A plain <ul> has nowhere to put it - either give the item a role that takes it (option, tab, row, treeitem) and implement that role’s keyboard contract, or drop the attribute.
A toolbar holds commands (Bold, Italic), not navigation, so it is not a <nav> landmark.
